payload.task_text:
I need a product ranking report from our SALES_DW data warehouse. Please query the orders and products data, focusing only on orders that have been delivered, and rank the products by total revenue within each product category. (The warehouse currently contains a single product category, so the rankings and category totals will cover that one category.)

Create an Excel file called "Product_Rankings.xlsx" in the workspace. The first sheet should be named "Rankings" with these columns: Category, Product_Name, Brand, Units_Sold, Revenue (rounded to 2 decimal places), and Rank_In_Category. Only include the top 5 products per category, ranked by revenue descending. Sort the rows by Category alphabetically and then by Rank_In_Category ascending. For Product_Name, use the full product name exactly as it appears in the PRODUCTS table — do not truncate or strip any suffix (e.g. text such as "with No Cost EMI ..."); product names are matched exactly. Rank each product by its own PRODUCT_ID (do not merge rows that happen to share the same product name).

Add a second sheet called "Category Totals" with columns: Category, Total_Products_Sold (sum of all units sold in that category, not just top 5), Total_Revenue (rounded to 2 decimal places, sum of all revenue in that category, not just top 5), and Top_Product (the name of the highest-revenue product in that category). Sort the rows by Total_Revenue in descending order.

Finally, create a Google Sheet titled "Product Rankings Dashboard" and populate it with the same data as the Rankings sheet from the Excel file.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, complete it directly in the main agent and dispatch no sub-agent. The warehouse can produce the complete product and category tables in two compact set-based queries, and both outputs consume the same small result.

Discover and verify `SALES_DW.PUBLIC.ORDERS` and `SALES_DW.PUBLIC.PRODUCTS`, then join on `PRODUCT_ID` and filter orders with exact `STATUS='Delivered'`. In one product-level query group by `p.PRODUCT_ID,p.PRODUCT_NAME,p.BRAND,p.CATEGORY`, returning `SUM(o.QUANTITY)` as units and `SUM(o.TOTAL_AMOUNT)` as revenue; never group by product name alone. Rank within each category by raw revenue descending, then `PRODUCT_ID` ascending for deterministic ties, and retain only ranks 1-5. In one category query over the same delivered population return each category's all-product unit sum, all-product revenue, and its highest-revenue product using the same tie rule. Reconcile the category sums independently against delivered-order quantity/revenue controls; round only displayed revenue to two decimals and preserve full product names exactly.

Resolve the runtime workspace dynamically. The main agent is the sole writer of `Product_Rankings.xlsx`: create exact `Rankings(Category,Product_Name,Brand,Units_Sold,Revenue,Rank_In_Category)` sorted category then rank, and `Category Totals(Category,Total_Products_Sold,Total_Revenue,Top_Product)` sorted raw total revenue descending; use literal values and read both complete ranges back.

In native parallel with the local workbook write, call `search_spreadsheets(query="Product Rankings Dashboard", max_results=100)` and locally exact-match names. Reuse exactly one match, call `create_spreadsheet(title="Product Rankings Dashboard")` once only if absent, and block rather than write when duplicate exact titles or an ambiguous create result exists. Own one sheet containing the exact Rankings headers/rows, use `update_cells` once for the complete rectangular payload, then call `get_spreadsheet_info` and `get_sheet_data` for read-back. Final acceptance requires cloud and local Rankings rows to agree cell-for-cell and category totals to reconcile; do not add a Wave.

You are a planning sub-agent. Decompose the following task into an ordered list of subtasks. For each subtask, specify:
- Dispatch decision: `self` (main agent), `explore`, or `coder`.
- Whether it is independent (parallelizable) or must wait on another subtask's output.

TASK DESCRIPTION (from the user):
"I need a product ranking report from our SALES_DW data warehouse. Please query the orders and products data, focusing only on orders that have been delivered, and rank the products by total revenue within each product category. (The warehouse currently contains a single product category, so the rankings and category totals will cover that one category.)

Create an Excel file called 'Product_Rankings.xlsx' in the workspace. The first sheet should be named 'Rankings' with these columns: Category, Product_Name, Brand, Units_Sold, Revenue (rounded to 2 decimal places), and Rank_In_Category. Only include the top 5 products per category, ranked by revenue descending. Sort the rows by Category alphabetically and then by Rank_In_Category ascending. For Product_Name, use the full product name exactly as it appears in the PRODUCTS table — do not truncate or strip any suffix (e.g. text such as 'with No Cost EMI ...'); product names are matched exactly. Rank each product by its own PRODUCT_ID (do not merge rows that happen to share the same product name).

Add a second sheet called 'Category Totals' with columns: Category, Total_Products_Sold (sum of all units sold in that category, not just top 5), Total_Revenue (rounded to 2 decimal places, sum of all revenue in that category, not just top 5), and Top_Product (the name of the highest-revenue product in that category). Sort the rows by Total_Revenue in descending order.

Finally, create a Google Sheet titled 'Product Rankings Dashboard' and populate it with the same data as the Rankings sheet from the Excel file."

CONTEXT YOU ALREADY HAVE:
- The workspace directory is: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-sf-sales-product-ranking-gsheet/workspace
- Available tools include: Snowflake MCP (list_databases, list_schemas, list_tables, describe_table, read_query), Excel MCP (create_workbook, create_worksheet, write_data_to_excel, rename_worksheet, read_data_from_excel, etc.), Google Sheets MCP (create_spreadsheet, create_sheet, update_cells, get_sheet_data, etc.), filesystem MCP, and python_execute.
- The task involves: (1) exploring the Snowflake SALES_DW warehouse to understand schema (orders, products tables, how "delivered" status is represented, category column), (2) writing SQL queries to compute revenue per product per category for delivered orders, (3) building the Excel file with two sheets, (4) creating/populating the Google Sheet dashboard, and (5) verifying results.

You may use read-only tools (Snowflake queries, filesystem reads, listing allowed directories) to inspect the environment if needed to make the plan concrete (e.g., confirm table names/schema in SALES_DW). Do NOT create or modify any files or external resources.

Deliverable: A concise, ordered subtask list with dispatch decisions, dependencies, and any specific SQL/logic notes (e.g., how to compute revenue — likely sum(quantity * price) or an existing revenue column — and how to filter delivered orders).
Plan product ranking task

You are a coder sub-agent. Build an Excel file `Product_Rankings.xlsx` in the workspace directory:
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-sf-sales-product-ranking-gsheet/workspace

CONTEXT: This is a product ranking report derived from the SALES_DW data warehouse (Snowflake, SALES_DW.PUBLIC schema). Orders have STATUS values including 'Delivered'. Products may share identical PRODUCT_NAME across distinct PRODUCT_IDs — you MUST aggregate by PRODUCT_ID so each product keeps its own row (do NOT merge rows sharing a name), and you MUST use the full PRODUCT_NAME exactly as returned by the query (do not truncate or strip any suffix such as 'with No Cost EMI & Additional Exchange Offers' or trailing '...').

STEP 1 — Run these two SQL queries via the Snowflake read_query tool:

Query A (Rankings — top 5 per category by revenue desc):
SELECT CATEGORY, PRODUCT_NAME, BRAND, UNITS_SOLD, REVENUE, RNK
FROM (
  SELECT p.CATEGORY, p.PRODUCT_NAME, p.BRAND,
         SUM(o.QUANTITY) AS UNITS_SOLD,
         ROUND(SUM(o.TOTAL_AMOUNT), 2) AS REVENUE,
         RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY p.CATEGORY ORDER BY SUM(o.TOTAL_AMOUNT) DESC) AS RNK
  FROM SALES_DW.PUBLIC.ORDERS o
  JOIN SALES_DW.PUBLIC.PRODUCTS p ON o.PRODUCT_ID = p.PRODUCT_ID
  WHERE o.STATUS = 'Delivered'
  GROUP BY p.CATEGORY, p.PRODUCT_ID, p.PRODUCT_NAME, p.BRAND
) t
WHERE RNK <= 5
ORDER BY CATEGORY, RNK;

Query B (Category Totals — all products in category, not just top 5):
SELECT t.CATEGORY, t.TOTAL_PRODUCTS_SOLD, t.TOTAL_REVENUE, p.PRODUCT_NAME AS TOP_PRODUCT
FROM (
  SELECT p.CATEGORY,
         SUM(o.QUANTITY) AS TOTAL_PRODUCTS_SOLD,
         ROUND(SUM(o.TOTAL_AMOUNT), 2) AS TOTAL_REVENUE
  FROM SALES_DW.PUBLIC.ORDERS o
  JOIN SALES_DW.PUBLIC.PRODUCTS p ON o.PRODUCT_ID = p.PRODUCT_ID
  WHERE o.STATUS = 'Delivered'
  GROUP BY p.CATEGORY
) t
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT p.CATEGORY, p.PRODUCT_NAME,
         RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY p.CATEGORY ORDER BY SUM(o.TOTAL_AMOUNT) DESC) AS RNK
  FROM SALES_DW.PUBLIC.ORDERS o
  JOIN SALES_DW.PUBLIC.PRODUCTS p ON o.PRODUCT_ID = p.PRODUCT_ID
  WHERE o.STATUS = 'Delivered'
  GROUP BY p.CATEGORY, p.PRODUCT_ID, p.PRODUCT_NAME
) p ON t.CATEGORY = p.CATEGORY AND p.RNK = 1
ORDER BY t.TOTAL_REVENUE DESC;

STEP 2 — Create the Excel workbook at:
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_deepseek-v4-flash/SingleUserTurn-sf-sales-product-ranking-gsheet/workspace/Product_Rankings.xlsx

Recommended: use mcp__local__python_execute with openpyxl for precise control (openpyxl is available). Alternatively use the Excel MCP tools (create_workbook, rename_worksheet, write_data_to_excel). Requirements:

- Sheet 1 named exactly "Rankings" with header row exactly: Category | Product_Name | Brand | Units_Sold | Revenue | Rank_In_Category
  - Data rows = Query A results (5 rows). Keep revenue as numeric rounded to 2 decimals (e.g., 79065.0 → 79065, 48927.16). Units_Sold as integer (92 not 92.0). Rank_In_Category as integer 1..5. Category string as-is. Product_Name and Brand exactly as returned (full names, untruncated).
- Sheet 2 named exactly "Category Totals" with header row exactly: Category | Total_Products_Sold | Total_Revenue | Top_Product
  - Data rows = Query B results (1 row). Total_Products_Sold integer, Total_Revenue numeric rounded to 2 decimals, Top_Product full name as-is.
- Rows are already sorted correctly by the queries (Category asc then Rank asc for sheet 1; Total_Revenue desc for sheet 2). Do not re-sort.
- Only these two sheets in the workbook (delete any default extra sheet).

STEP 3 — Verify by reading back with the Excel MCP tool read_data_from_excel on both sheets. Confirm: sheet names, headers, row counts (5 data rows + 1 header for Rankings; 1 data row + 1 header for Category Totals), revenue rounded to 2 decimals, and that product names are complete (spot-check that the rank-1 name ends with 'with No Cost EMI & Additional Exchange Offers').

SANITY CHECK (expected values from the validated baseline):
- Rankings: rank 1 = 'Samsung Galaxy S20 FE 5G (Cloud Navy, 8GB RAM, 128GB Storage) with No Cost EMI & Additional Exchange Offers', Units 92, Revenue 79065.0; rank 2 'OnePlus 11 5G (Titan Black, 16GB RAM, 256GB Storage)' 70 / 48927.16; rank 3 'OnePlus 10R 5G (Forest Green, 12GB RAM, 256GB Storage, 80W SuperVOOC)' 89 / 43517.02; rank 4 'Samsung 108 cm (43 inches) Crystal 4K Neo Series Ultra HD Smart LED TV UA43AUE65AKXXL (Black)' 79 / 41436.49; rank 5 'Samsung 108 cm (43 inches) Crystal 4K Series Ultra HD Smart LED TV UA43AUE60AKLXL (Black)' 67 / 39356.41. Category for all: 'tv, audio & cameras'.
- Category Totals: 29915 / 2177149.66 / top product = same as rank-1 name.

DELIVERABLE: Report the absolute file path, the exact sheet names, and the full content written to each sheet (all rows verbatim). Do not create any files other than Product_Rankings.xlsx.
Build Product_Rankings.xlsx

You are a coder sub-agent. Create a Google Spreadsheet titled "Product Rankings Dashboard" and populate it with product ranking data derived from the SALES_DW data warehouse (Snowflake, SALES_DW.PUBLIC schema). The data must match the "Rankings" sheet content of an Excel report: header row + top 5 products per category (the warehouse has a single category).

CONTEXT: Orders have STATUS values including 'Delivered'. Products may share identical PRODUCT_NAME across distinct PRODUCT_IDs — aggregate by PRODUCT_ID (do NOT merge rows sharing a name) and use the full PRODUCT_NAME exactly as returned by the query (do not truncate or strip any suffix such as 'with No Cost EMI & Additional Exchange Offers').

STEP 1 — Run this SQL query via the Snowflake read_query tool:

SELECT CATEGORY, PRODUCT_NAME, BRAND, UNITS_SOLD, REVENUE, RNK
FROM (
  SELECT p.CATEGORY, p.PRODUCT_NAME, p.BRAND,
         SUM(o.QUANTITY) AS UNITS_SOLD,
         ROUND(SUM(o.TOTAL_AMOUNT), 2) AS REVENUE,
         RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY p.CATEGORY ORDER BY SUM(o.TOTAL_AMOUNT) DESC) AS RNK
  FROM SALES_DW.PUBLIC.ORDERS o
  JOIN SALES_DW.PUBLIC.PRODUCTS p ON o.PRODUCT_ID = p.PRODUCT_ID
  WHERE o.STATUS = 'Delivered'
  GROUP BY p.CATEGORY, p.PRODUCT_ID, p.PRODUCT_NAME, p.BRAND
) t
WHERE RNK <= 5
ORDER BY CATEGORY, RNK;

STEP 2 — Using the Google Sheets MCP tools:
- create_spreadsheet with title exactly "Product Rankings Dashboard". Capture the returned spreadsheet_id.
- Populate the default sheet with header row exactly: Category | Product_Name | Brand | Units_Sold | Revenue | Rank_In_Category, followed by the 5 data rows from the query (in the query's returned order — already sorted by Category asc, Rank asc). Rename the default sheet tab to "Rankings" (rename_sheet) so the tab clearly identifies the content.
- Values: Category and Product_Name and Brand as exact strings; Units_Sold as integer (92 not 92.0); Revenue as numeric rounded to 2 decimals (79065.0 → 79065, 48927.16 stays 48927.16); Rank_In_Category as integer 1..5.
- Use update_cells (or batch_update_cells) with range A1:F6 covering header + 5 rows.

STEP 3 — Verify by reading back with get_sheet_data: confirm the spreadsheet title, the sheet name, header row, and all 5 data rows match the query output exactly.

SANITY CHECK (expected values):

- Rank 1: 'Samsung Galaxy S20 FE 5G (Cloud Navy, 8GB RAM, 128GB Storage) with No Cost EMI & Additional Exchange Offers' | LG | 92 | 79065
- Rank 2: 'OnePlus 11 5G (Titan Black, 16GB RAM, 256GB Storage)' | Bose | 70 | 48927.16
- Rank 3: 'OnePlus 10R 5G (Forest Green, 12GB RAM, 256GB Storage, 80W SuperVOOC)' | Apple | 89 | 43517.02
- Rank 4: 'Samsung 108 cm (43 inches) Crystal 4K Neo Series Ultra HD Smart LED TV UA43AUE65AKXXL (Black)' | Lenovo | 79 | 41436.49
- Rank 5: 'Samsung 108 cm (43 inches) Crystal 4K Series Ultra HD Smart LED TV UA43AUE60AKLXL (Black)' | Microsoft | 67 | 39356.41

DELIVERABLE: Report the spreadsheet_id, the exact spreadsheet title, the sheet tab name, and the full populated content (all rows verbatim). Do not create or modify any other external resources.
